g.text: 1) Functional Requirements:

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - RL should be able to identify clients by user ID, IP address, API key

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: to apply appropriate limits.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Limit Http requests based on configurable rules(100 requests per min).

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - When limits are exceeded, system should reject requests with http

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: 429 and include helpful header.

g.text: 1) 429 status code: Too Many requests, you've sent too many requests to a server

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: in a short time, triggering a rate limit to prevent overload or abuse.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: 2) Where should we place the rate limiter.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Bad Solution: Alongside the server

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Issue: servers are not aware of the global request count, hence the rate limiting

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: will be off by many folds.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Good Solution: Dedicated service

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Issues: Latency overhead of service calls, point of failure. Decide for fail

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: open(allow all the requests to go through) or fail closed (reject all the requests,

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: essentially taking your API offline). dedicated health checks required and for each

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: new service we need to integrate ratelimiting part.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Great Solution: API Gateway

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Challenges: limited Context about the request, storing RL state requires

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: external dependency on in-memory store like redis

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: 3) How do we identify clients.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - userId, IP address, API key: In reality we can use a combination of these

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: three.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Per-user limits: "Alice can make 1000 requests/hour"

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Per-IP limits: "This IP can make 100 requests/minute"

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Global limits: "Our API can handle 50,000 requests/second total"

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Endpoint-specific limits: "The search API is limited to 10 requests/minute, but

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: profile updates are 100/minute

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: 5) The state about the token bucket needs to be shared across all the intances

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: of the gateway. We use redis as central sourrce of truth for all token budcket

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: state. Note that there is going to be dual race conditions that needs to be taken

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: care of.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: RC1 : Request arrives, reads the current bucket tocken count and accordingly

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: updates it via atomic operation. here the update part is taken care of

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: RC2 : two different requests come at same time and reads same quantity, to

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: deal with this we can make the whole read-calculate-update logic part of a single

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: atomic transaction.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: 6) Limit is exceeded what now?

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: we have two options to deal with this.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: a) fail - fast, simply return 429 along with error headers

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: b) Queue the requests for later processing once the tokens are refilled. : this

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: approach is not a good approach for most of the cases. why ? queueing requests

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: can take up alot of memory

text.font-family: Lilita One, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: 2) Non Functional Requirements (SPARCS):

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Scalability: 1M RPS, 100M DAU

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Latency: Since there will be some latency in terms of the usual API call,

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: we don't want to add additional RL latency on top of it. hence (<10ms)

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Throughput: high through put should be taken care of.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Availability >> consistency

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: For this breakdown we are going to design request level rate limiting for social media platform's API

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: 1) Scalability to 1M rps: the current single node redis can take upto 100k

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: rps hence we will require around 10 nodes to take care of this. for that we

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: will be doing sharding based on the key. Now inorder to make sure every

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: time user a's request goes to shard A and vice versa we can use sething

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: like consistent hashing. At production lvl this is done via something called

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: reddis cluster. -- need to read more about it.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: 2) Availability & fault tolerance: What happens when one of the shard goes

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: down. all the users specific to that shard gets effected. for such cases we

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: can pick on of the two apprroaches fail - closed or fail -open. But better

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: thing would be to ensure we dont come to this. for that we could have

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: replicas for the redis nodes and Inorder to deal with latency issue we can

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: use the async syncing of replicas.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: 3) latency: While the redis resp time is less, the network call to and fro

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: from redis would take some time(20-50ms) due to the tcp handshake

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: overhead for each request. we can solve this issue by using a connection

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: pool of persistent connections. another big win would be geographical

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: distribution of the rate limiting infra near to the user.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - legit high volume clients: equest queueing

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - abusive traffic: DDOS protection, temporary blocking of the ip/API

g.text: key
